title: Ang 938–946: the Sidh Gosht
tomorrow: why would a Guru borrow the tune of a war ballad?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 929: Oankar, the letters as a ladder to the Name. Today, a conversation on a mountain, and the whole week gathered up.
screen: `LETTERS, A LADDER TO THE NAME.` → `A WEEK GATHERED.`

segments.voice: Sooner or later every podcast guest gets the same question: who were your mentors? Ang 938 opens on that question, asked by yogis. The Sidh Gosht, the discussion with the Siddhas: Guru Nanak among wandering yogis who had left the world behind. Tradition places them in the mountains. They test him with question after question, about the road, the self, the way out. And then the big one: who is your guru? Whose disciple are you?
screen: `WHO WERE YOUR MENTORS?` → `YOGIS TEST GURU NANAK.` → `WHO IS YOUR GURU?`

segments.voice: Guru Nanak's answer, on ang 943, in paraphrase: the Shabad, the Word, is the Guru; the attention tuned to it, surat, is the disciple. Not a person on a seat. The Word. And the one who learns isn't even the whole self; it's the listening part. The yogis had left homes and work behind to look for truth on the heights. Guru Nanak's answer brings it back down: the Word can be heard wherever a person truly listens, in a kitchen as well as on a mountain. It's the line under this whole walk through the Granth, and part of why the Granth itself is honored as Guru. Now the week, page by page. Two Gurus in one raga, both signing Nanak. A hymn of many names, Ram and Khuda at one table, and the hukam beneath. The Anand, with its party and its ease. The Sadd: sing, don't weep. The chhants, where the dear Friend stands close. Oankar, the alphabet as a ladder. And today, the yogis' question, answered with the Word. Seven days in Ramkali, and each turned out to be about what a person listens to.
screen: `THE SHABAD IS THE GURU.` · `SURAT, ATTENTION, IS THE DISCIPLE.` · `A WEEK IN RAMKALI.` · then, large: `THE WORD IS GURU.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and choose one sound in the room: a fan, traffic, your own breath. Give it your whole attention, the way surat leans toward the Word. When the mind wanders off, notice, and come back to the sound.
Ang 938. Where the Sidh Gosht begins: Guru Nanak with the yogis, and the answer that the Word is the Guru.
The word is guru, and the listening is the student. A good week in Ramkali.

howItsDone: Sikhs read the Sidh Gosht in Ramkali and often quote its line that the Shabad is the Guru and the attention tuned to it is the disciple; it is one reason the Granth is honored as Guru.
